title: Section 1557 & AI Translation: September 2026
summary: Section 1557 requires language access for LEP patients. See how AI translation helps health leaders meet compliance goals. September 2026.
body_markdown:
###


Yes. Opalite integrates with Epic, Cerner/Oracle Health, eClinicalWorks, athenahealth, MEDITECH, Allscripts, and NextGen. The Epic integration supports native launch directly from a patient chart in under five seconds, with automatic patient-language detection, note transfer, and encounter logging. Deeper integrations pass patient context, write encounter notes, and log interpreter credentials per encounter, the detail OCR weighs most in a documentation review. Before selecting a vendor, confirm what the integration actually does: single sign-on alone is not the same as full encounter documentation. Ask for a specific integration specification and check whether it is in active clinical use at comparable organizations.


###


AI interpretation can reduce interpretation spending by more than 50% compared with traditional per-minute services. Two factors drive most of the savings: lower per-minute rates and no charges for silent time during physical exams, chart review, or pauses in conversation. For organizations running hundreds of interpreted encounters per month, the silent-time difference alone adds up quickly. Actual savings depend on your current vendor rates, usage volume, and contract terms.


###


Yes. AI interpretation is available instantly, around the clock, across more than 150 languages and dialects, with no scheduling, queuing, or waiting for an interpreter to connect. That coverage matters most for rare languages and after-hours encounters where traditional phone interpreter services can have long connection times. Organizations running telehealth programs or covering overnight shifts no longer need to depend on interpreter availability windows.


###


Start with compliance basics: a signed Business Associate Agreement, encryption in transit and at rest, and written confirmation of whether patient data is used for model training. Then move to clinical fit: ask whether the system was trained on medical conversations or adapted from a general consumer model, and request any independent validation data. For workflow integration, confirm EHR compatibility, encounter logging, and audit trail capabilities. Finally, ask about quality controls: what the vendor does when the system produces a low-confidence output, and how errors are caught and reviewed.


###


Section 1557 permits AI translation across communication types and sets a quality standard for content that affects a patient's rights, benefits, or meaningful access to care. Validated AI quality controls meet that standard; a separate human review step is not required when those controls are in place. The 2024 final rule, effective July 5, 2024, requires covered entities with 15 or more staff to designate a Section 1557 coordinator, maintain written language access policies, and post a Notice of Availability in the 15 most commonly spoken languages in their state. OCR weighs documentation of interpreter credentials per encounter most heavily in a review. An AI interpretation tool that logs the interpreter, the language, and the encounter automatically satisfies that documentation requirement without manual entry.
